recentItems.title: 'I didn't know Liberia existed' - deported to Africa by Trump
recentItems.description:
Arrested by ICE and deported to West Africa - this is how Donald Trump's immigration crackdown is sending people to countries they've never heard of.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

According to information collected by human rights groups, the Trump administration has agreements with at least 35 third countries - some of the world's poorest - to take in deportees from the United States who can't be returned to their original countries.


About 25,000 people have been scooped up and sent to a variety of third countries - including Liberia - where Channel 4 News found deportees from Latin America with no idea what to do now, unable to speak the language and separated from family in the US.

The Trump administration is proud of its aggressive immigration policy and intends it to be a deterrent. August saw a new high in arrests by ICE, reaching nearly 51,000. It is now increasingly deporting people to third countries, describing it as a “show of force”, intended to make people fear the consequences of entering the US without permission.

For those affected it is a sentence that leaves them in limbo, thousands of miles from their families and the lives they had built in the United States.

recentItems.title: How to REVIVE the UK’s economy -  from a former Bank of England economist
recentItems.description:
Can Andy Burnham turn the UK economy around?

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

With just a few weeks to go until his first Budget, the new prime minister is facing a difficult economic outlook, as he deals with sluggish growth, the rising cost of living and a war in Iran which threatens to send inflation soaring. 

In this episode of The Fourcast, Krishnan Guru-Murthy speaks to the former chief economist of the Bank of England Andy Haldane and Channel 4’s Economics Editor Helia Ebrahimi.

They discuss cuts to welfare, the pensions triple lock and Britain’s problem with young NEETS: those not in education, employment or training.
